newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African currency held up against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, maintaining a narrow range despite repeated attempts to weaken it.
"It's holding ground at the moment," one dealer said. The rand was last at 4.5545/75 against the dollar from 4.5535/5565 late on Monday, rebuffing an intra-day push to 4.5575.

Local demand for dollars helped to slightly weaken the rand soon after the opening on Tuesday in a directionless market, but dealers said the central bank stepped in to cap undue pressure on the currency at around the 4.5550-4.5575 level.

The market was seen to be nervous on the back of jittery offshore emerging markets and the prospect of the gold price coming down further and adversely affecting the country's current account deficit.
Cross rate action showed the local unit withstood the dollar's strength better than some offshore currencies.
The rand was trading at 7.6016/6112 against sterling from 7.6900/6973 previously and at 25.2979/3366 yen from 24.9159/9500 on Monday.
But the rand did not fare as well against the mark, having last changed hands at 0.3948/3953 marks, down slightly from Monday's 1400 GMT close of 0.3950/3955.
Bonds strengthened slightly late on Tuesday after jobber activity saw yields hit an intraday high of 14.365 bid.
The benchmark R150 recovered to 14.265 percent by the local close from Monday's 14.31 percent on institutional demand after a failed assault on the 14.35 percent ceiling.
In the morning session, traders said that while foreign interest had dwindled, some jobbers had been caught long and had started squaring off their positions.
After midday, however, bonds had begun recouping the morning's losses as jobbers collectively started to cover.
One trader attributed the day's swings to "the nervousness of the unconvinced bulls."
Although a sideways move was anticipated for Wednesday, the overall trend on the bond market was seen remaining strong.
"In the short term we could see it weaken further, but it's still a long term buy. The main bull trend is still intact," one trader said.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 7.757 billion rand on Monday from 7.360 billion rand on Saturday.
Foreigners were net sellers 330.49 million rand's worth of bonds on Monday after buying 285.38 million rand's worth on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
The total value of Monday's Bond Exchange turnover fell to 3.99 billion rand on Monday from 5.9 billion rand on Friday.
